industry: Electronic Manufacturing Services / Data Center Infrastructure
thesis: Celestica is a technology manufacturing leader whose Connectivity & Cloud Solutions segment is rapidly becoming a pure-play AI data center infrastructure company. Q2 2026 revenue surged 62% YoY to $4.70B with GAAP EPS of $3.17 and adjusted EPS of $2.54, both exceeding guidance. FY2025 revenue was $12.39B (+28.5%) with FY2026 TTM run-rate now at ~$15.6B. The company's deep engineering expertise in 400G/800G networking switches, AI server rack integration, and high-power compute platforms has made it a critical partner for hyperscalers. At ~41x P/E the stock is richly valued, but revenue momentum and margin expansion justify a BUY. The one-year target of ~$678 from analysts implies significant upside.

drivers: AI server and networking switch demand accelerates as hyperscaler capex continues to grow
Margin expansion from higher-value AI compute and networking content mix
800G/1.6T networking switch manufacturing ramps expand Celestica's wallet share
Enterprise AI adoption creates a second demand wave beyond hyperscalers

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 revenue reaches ~$18–19B with adjusted operating margin near 8%, and adjusted EPS of ~$10–11. Market applies a 40–45x multiple, reflecting strong but decelerating growth. Stock trades near current levels.

risks: Hyperscaler AI capex pause compresses order visibility and revenue growth
Customer concentration risk — loss of a major hyperscaler customer would be material
EMS/ODM industry margin compression from competition with Foxconn and Quanta
Macro slowdown or tariff disruptions impact global supply chain operations

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — revenue $4.70B (+62% YoY), adjusted EPS $2.54, guidance beat
Q3 2026 earnings — AI compute and networking mix trends
800G/1.6T networking switch and next-gen AI server platform ramps

key_risks: Customer concentration: hyperscaler customers represent a dominant share of Connectivity & Cloud revenue
EMS/ODM margins are structurally thin; margin expansion depends on mix shift to higher-value AI content
Cyclical exposure to hyperscaler capex cycles — any spending pause would hit revenue hard
Competition from larger ODMs (Foxconn, Quanta, Wistron) could limit pricing power
Stock has rallied ~60% over the last year, limiting near-term risk/reward from current levels
